reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it presents a PancakeSwap/BSC front-running or sniper bot as a way to make unusually large profits and instructs viewers to deploy or operate a contract, fund it with BNB, and start automated trades and profit transfers. The speaker cites returns including several hundred BNB in recent weeks, an approximately 15-times result, and up to 100 BNB per day, although the supplied records do not independently verify the contract behavior or profits. A visible BscScan savings advertisement is separate from the video's bot solicitation because the frame does not establish that the creator operates, endorses, or connects the banner to the contract.

citations.quote: Make huge profits With a Sniper Bot Easy Tutorial
Today I'm going to be going over deploying a front-running bot on pancake swap with a Wrapped BNB pair.
immediately buy and sell at profit
send some funds to that contract
press the action button

opening.argument: The presentation itself includes a material risk warning rather than an unconditional promise. It explains that token burn fees and gas costs can exceed returns, identifies a threshold below which the contract may lose money, and recommends additional funding to reduce that specific operational risk. That qualification is inconsistent with portraying the outcome as guaranteed. The description also presents a defined allocation model in which profits are divided between the wallet and continued operation, giving viewers concrete mechanics to evaluate rather than merely asserting effortless income.

citations.quote: the contract will basically waste in fees more than make profit
I recommend funding the contract with around 1 - 0.5 BNB just to make sure that won't happen.
10% of profit automatically reenters the front-run pool
automatically transacts back to your wallet 90% of the profit

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution emphasizes promotional returns, but that does not erase the explicit warning that fees can exceed gains. Its quoted funding instruction shows participation in a demonstration, not a guarantee that every user will profit. The description specifically identifies adverse token-fee conditions and explains how they affect results, which is the kind of limitation a deceptive unconditional offer would omit.

citations.quote: nowadays most of tokens comes with 3~6% fees
If you fund the contract with 0.4 BNB or less
I've had really good luck with this.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The warning is a limited operational caveat, not a neutral disclosure of the central risk. The same material still says the system will buy and sell at profit, and the speaker claims unusually large personal returns. Explaining that insufficient funds may be consumed by fees does not substantiate that the contract can deliver the promoted profits or safely return deposited BNB.

citations.quote: immediately buy and sell at profit
In the last few weeks, I've made several hundred BNB
it's already around 15 times

opening.argument: The content is presented as an operational programming tutorial: it walks through creating a Solidity file, compiling it in Remix, connecting injected Web3, and inspecting the deployed contract. The title itself calls it an “Easy Tutorial,” while the narration explains implementation components such as the wrapped BNB address and Pancake router. A demonstration of blockchain deployment and automated trading mechanics can be educational even when the presenter discusses a claimed result; the supplied material does not independently establish that the code performs as described or that the result is representative.

citations.quote: Easy Tutorial
we're going to build our contract
Let me go compile the frontrun bot.
We're gonna do injected Web3.

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling it a tutorial is supported by the actual workflow: the speaker creates, compiles, deploys, and examines a contract. The prosecution treats every instructional step as solicitation, but the quoted material establishes a technical demonstration and does not independently verify either the contract's behavior or the claimed returns. Discussing how a tool operates is not itself proof that its claims are certified.

citations.quote: This is where we're going to build our contract.
we have our deployment utility
we can see that it's in the address there now.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The tutorial framing cannot separate the technical steps from the requested financial action. The speaker tells viewers to fund the deployed contract, activate it, and expects a deposit back, then presents the result as a repeatable profit cycle. Code and deployment screens show activity, but they do not prove that the promised automated trading or returns are legitimate.

citations.quote: I'm just gonna do 0.5 BNB
press the action button
We usually only need to wait a couple of minutes before we get back a deposit
you can run this cycle multiple times a day

opening.argument: The material describes a software-based service and its operating procedure, not a downline or credential-harvesting scheme. The stated workflow uses public developer tools and a wallet connection: viewers are directed to Remix, MetaMask, and Binance Smart Chain, while the contract is deployed and viewed through BSC Scan. The supplied instructions do not ask viewers to surrender a password or private key, recruit others, or pay a subscription. The description also identifies transaction fees and token burn fees as ordinary costs that can affect a trading operation.

citations.quote: Access Remix: https://remix.ethereum.org/
Get MetaMask: https://metamask.io/download.html
Connect MetaMask to Binance Smart Chain
we can see that it's in the address there now.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution identifies a funded contract, but funding a blockchain trading tool is not by itself proof of a scam mechanism. The supplied workflow shows a public wallet transaction and contract address, with costs attributed to gas and token fees. It contains no instruction to provide a password, private key, or referral payment. The high-return language can be promotional commentary without establishing that the service is fraudulent.

citations.quote: We paid a little gas.
just adds liquidity within Pancake Swap
possible burn fees

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The absence of a password request does not resolve the core mechanism: viewers are told to send BNB directly to a deployed contract and activate it for purported profits. Public tooling and a visible address establish only that a transaction occurred, not that funds will be returned. The speaker's claims of fifteen-times results and up to one hundred BNB per day make this more than ordinary software promotion.

citations.quote: I'm just gonna do 0.5 BNB.
then it gives it generally
you can have upwards of hundred BNB a day
